# Packet — ani-hymn-to-ra: Hymn to Ra at his rising

Established from Budge 1895, pp. 1–5. Start: {"page": 1, "plate": "I", "line": 1, "note": "Under the heading PLATE I: \"ṭua Rā χeft uben - f\" (Adoration of Rā when riseth he); ṭua and χeft … ābtet overlined (red)."}. End: {"page": 5, "plate": "I", "line": 28, "lastWord": "Àni", "note": "... to the ka of Osiris Ani. (immediately above the italic heading \"Appendix.\" on p. 5)"}.
Left out as not Ani's text: p. 1: footnote 1, "Characters over which a line is printed are, in the papyrus, written in red."; p. 3: footnote 1 (on ut'a - à, l. 14): "The papyrus has" A1 G43 U28 — the papyrus sets the seated man before ut'a; Budge prints it after; p. 4: footnote 1 (on the first ànt, l. 15): the Leyden Papyrus of Qenna has a fuller text here; Budge would add after Ani's ànt the words "in revolution" (Naville, Todtenbuch, Bl. xiv, ll. 13–14); p. 5: the section headed "Appendix." [British Museum Papyrus, No. 10,471] (the hymn of Nekht) and what follows to p. 7.

One line per word of the established text, in order: index · page/plate/line · signs (code=character, * = not yet in the sign glossary: add it with signs.py before building) · layout · Budge's transliteration · Budge's English (his 1895 understanding: a check on sense, never wording) · flags.
Your units must use these signs in exactly this order (the build compares the whole sequence); you may join or split Budge's word groups where the grammar requires (say so in the note when you do).
